title: Crisis Management
completion_message: ¡Excelente! Resolver crisis requiere cabeza fría y vocabulario afilado. Sabes cómo manejar el control de daños y evitar un desastre de relaciones públicas.

parts.visual:
El vocabulario de los momentos más oscuros de una empresa. 

1. Damage control (Control de daños): 
- Medidas tomadas para minimizar el daño a la reputación tras un escándalo o error. 
Ej: After the CEO's racist tweet, the PR team went into DAMAGE CONTROL. 

2. PR disaster (Desastre de Relaciones Públicas): 
- Un evento que destruye la imagen pública de la empresa. 
Ej: Selling exploding batteries was a massive PR DISASTER. 

3. Scapegoat (Chivo expiatorio): 
- Una persona culpada por las fallas o errores de otros. 
Ej: The junior manager was used as a SCAPEGOAT to protect the CEO.
parts.audio: Welcome to Corporate Crisis Management. The vocabulary for a company's darkest moments. Number 1: Damage control. Measures taken to minimize damage to a company's reputation after a scandal or mistake. For example: After the CEO's racist tweet, the PR team went into DAMAGE CONTROL. Number 2: PR disaster. PR stands for Public Relations. A PR disaster is an event that destroys the public image of a company. For example: Selling exploding batteries was a massive PR DISASTER. Number 3: Scapegoat. A person who is blamed for the wrongdoings, mistakes, or faults of others. For example: The junior manager was used as a SCAPEGOAT to protect the CEO.

parts.visual:
4. Fall guy (El que asume la culpa): 
- Similar al scapegoat, alguien dispuesto a cargar con la culpa (a menudo a cambio de dinero o para proteger la organización). 
Ej: He was paid millions to be the FALL GUY and go to jail. 

5. Sweep under the rug (Barrer bajo la alfombra): 
- Ocultar un problema o escándalo en lugar de enfrentarlo. 
Ej: They tried to SWEEP the harassment allegations UNDER THE RUG. 

6. Backlash (Reacción violenta / Respuesta negativa severa): 
- Una fuerte reacción pública negativa contra una empresa o decisión. 
Ej: The new policy caused a massive BACKLASH from customers. 

7. Boycott (Boicot): 
- Cuando el público se niega colectivamente a comprar o usar un producto como protesta. 
Ej: Activists called for a BOYCOTT of the brand.
parts.audio: Number 4: Fall guy. Similar to a scapegoat, but often someone who agrees to take the blame, sometimes for a financial reward or loyalty to the organization. For example: He was paid millions to be the FALL GUY and go to jail. Number 5: Sweep under the rug. To hide a problem or keep a scandal secret instead of dealing with it openly. For example: They tried to SWEEP the harassment allegations UNDER THE RUG. Number 6: Backlash. A strong and adverse reaction by a large number of people, especially to a social or political development. For example: The new policy caused a massive BACKLASH from customers. Finally, Number 7: Boycott. When the public collectively refuses to buy or use a product as a protest. For example: Activists called for a BOYCOTT of the brand.

stages.title: Interactive Quiz
stages.description: Elige el término correcto de gestión de crisis.

questions.question: The factory leaked chemicals into the river. The PR team is now doing damage ____ to save our reputation.
The marketing campaign was deeply offensive to many people. It turned into a massive ____ disaster. (Relaciones Públicas).
questions.explanation: PR disaster = Desastre de Public Relations.

questions.question: The board of directors made the bad decision, but they fired the project manager as a ____ so the public would blame him instead.
He agreed to be the ____ guy, taking all the legal blame for the fraud in exchange for a secret payment.
questions.explanation: Fall guy = el que asume la culpa/cae por los demás.

questions.question: You can't just sweep this corruption scandal under the ____. The press will find out eventually. (Barrer bajo la alfombra).
questions.explanation: Sweep under the rug = ocultar bajo la alfombra.

questions.question: When they raised the price of the life-saving medicine by 500%, they faced a massive public ____. (Reacción negativa severa).
questions.explanation: Backlash = reacción violenta de la opinión pública.

questions.question: Because of the company's terrible environmental record, millions of consumers joined a ____ and stopped buying their products.
To issue a formal, public statement saying you are sorry for a mistake is to issue an ____.
questions.explanation: Issue an apology = emitir una disculpa formal.

questions.question: A situation where employees refuse to work as a form of organized protest is a ____. (Huelga).
To take full responsibility for a mistake or failure is to ____ the blame. (Asumir la culpa).
questions.explanation: Take the blame (o shoulder the blame) = asumir la culpa.

questions.question: To unfairly blame someone else for a mistake you made is to ____ the blame.
questions.explanation: Shift the blame = desviar la culpa hacia otro.

questions.question: When a company discovers a dangerous defect in its cars, it must issue a product ____ to bring them back to the factory.
questions.explanation: Product recall = retiro del mercado por defectos.

questions.question: A sudden, unexpected problem that causes a lot of damage is a ____. (Desastre/Catástrofe).
To limit or stop the spread of bad news or a crisis is to ____ it. (Contener).
questions.explanation: Contain the crisis = contener la crisis.

questions.question: If you try to cover up a crime, the ____ is often worse than the crime itself. (Encubrimiento).
To voluntarily leave your job, especially after a scandal, is to ____. (Renunciar/Dimitir).
A person hired specifically to handle public relations during a scandal and 'spin' the news positively is a ____ doctor.
questions.explanation: Spin doctor = experto en PR que manipula o suaviza las noticias.

questions.question: An official investigation into a company's financial records to find missing money is an ____.
If the company doesn't survive the crisis, it will have to file for ____. (Bancarrota).
When facing a crisis, the worst thing a CEO can do is bury their head in the ____ and ignore it. (Esconder la cabeza como el avestruz).
questions.explanation: Bury your head in the sand = ignorar el problema esperando que desaparezca.

stages.title: Written Expression

questions.question: Damage ____. (Control de daños con C)
A massive ____ disaster. (Relaciones públicas con P)
He was the ____. (Chivo expiatorio con S)
The ____ guy. (El que asume la culpa con F)
Sweep it under the ____. (Barrer bajo la alfombra con R)
A public ____. (Reacción negativa severa con B)
A consumer ____. (Boicot con B)
A product ____. (Retiro del mercado por defectos con R)
The ____ is worse than the crime. (Encubrimiento con C)
Bury your head in the ____. (Ignorar el problema con S)
